programme: An arterial/endothelial-specification and VEGF-responsive angiogenic transcriptional module: SOX17 sets arterial endothelial identity, HOXB5 drives the ANGPT2/KDR (VEGFR2) sprouting axis, YAP1 (Hippo pathway effector) converts mechanical and growth-factor cues into pro-angiogenic transcription, and HTATIP2/TIP30 acts as a brake on VEGFA-driven neovascularization.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease this module underlies vessel-wall homeostasis and pathological angiogenesis/remodeling: arterial endothelial specification (SOX17), VEGFR2-driven neovascularization in ischemia and atherosclerotic plaque (the ANGPT2/KDR axis HOXB5 targets), and Hippo/YAP1 mechanotransduction in endothelium exposed to altered shear stress. None of this is placed here by Open Targets or the retrieved literature for any of the four factors — it is domain-general vascular biology, not a hit in this record.
role_in_b: In glioblastoma the same axis runs tumor neovascularization, which the tumor depends on for growth: YAP1-dependent angiogenesis and Hippo-pathway signaling in glioma, HOXB5 as a prognostic marker tied to a proliferative/vascular gene program, and HTATIP2 as an epigenetically silenced angiogenesis restraint whose loss promotes treatment resistance. This side is directly documented in the retrieved papers.
shared_axis: Both diseases are angiogenesis-dependent: cardiovascular disease through vessel remodeling and ischemia-driven neovascularization, glioblastoma through tumor-driven neovascularization that the tumor cannot grow past a few millimeters without. A shared arterial-endothelial/VEGF-responsive transcriptional module recurring in both is consistent with that shared dependence on the same angiogenic machinery, deployed in different tissue contexts.
reasoning: The module is nameable and, on the glioblastoma side, independently placed by four papers spanning three of the four carrying factors (YAP1, HOXB5, HTATIP2); SOX17's glioblastoma placement is weak (ambiguous papers, modest percentile). Nothing was retrieved for cardiovascular disease for any of the twelve factors, so the cross-disease link rests on general knowledge that angiogenesis is central to both diseases, not on anything retrieved here — hence moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 35502183 — HOXB5 expression as a poor-prognosis biomarker in glioblastoma; PMID 33858489 — SRSF1/circATP5B/miR-185-5p/HOXB5 feedback loop in glioma stem cell proliferation; PMID 42568372 — Amotl2 phosphorylation promoting YAP1 signalling and glioma growth; PMID 42650824 — Honokiol disrupting SUMO1-YAP1 conjugation in glioma; PMID 42507234 — YAP-dependent angiogenesis in glioblastoma; PMID 42014897 — Hippo/YAP1 effector inhibition in glioma cells in vitro; PMID 37491696 — epigenetic silencing of HTATIP2 in glioblastoma enhancing treatment resistance.
how_to_falsify: In an endothelial-specific SOX17/YAP1 knockout or HTATIP2 restoration mouse model of vascular injury (e.g., hindlimb ischemia or atherosclerosis), and in a matched patient-derived glioblastoma vascular co-culture or xenograft with the same perturbations, test whether ANGPT2/KDR-driven sprouting and VEGFA output move concordantly. If glioblastoma vasculature depends on this module while cardiovascular endothelium does not respond to the same perturbations, the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood vs. brain; the 64 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the effective independent evidence is much smaller than 64. No Open Targets or literature evidence was retrieved for cardiovascular disease for any of the twelve concordant factors — the cardiovascular side of this account is reasoning from general vascular biology, not from anything in this record. Generic vascular/immune regulators (KLF2, ERG, NR3C1, FOS, STAT3, and others) were removed as tissue-generic before ranking, which is why no more 'obvious' vascular master regulator appears here — its absence is the exclusion working as intended, not a gap in the account. Factors that led only a single patient group (including KLF2's near-generic recurrence at 0.5) were excluded to avoid basing the story on one subgroup. Other listed factors (TFAP2E, TLX2, TRERF1, MLXIPL, IRX4, DAXX, LRRFIP1, HAND2) were not used to carry this programme because their documented functions (steroidogenesis, lipogenesis, autonomic neural crest specification, apoptosis) do not fit the angiogenic axis as cleanly, even though some overlap with it is plausible.
